messages:
Ken (Customer): hey team, hitting a bunch of 429s the last 30m after we had a failover to eu-west-1. latency is fine but requests are being rejected with `rate_limit_exceeded`. our app scaled up and basically all traffic shifted to eu-west and then started getting throttled.

Ken (Customer): example response header from our client: `status: 429`, `x-rw-region: eu-west-1`, `x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 14`. no obvious spike in token usage on our side, but the surge was a short burst ~5k req/min.

Ava (Support): thanks @Ken — sorry about that. Im going to triage with SRE. can you paste the account/org id and the route you were hitting? also did you see a `Retry-After` header? :thinking_face:

Ken (Customer): org: rw-corp-402, endpoint: POST /v1/generate (model: rw-large). we did see `Retry-After: 10`. attaching our minimal repro curl below.

Ken (Customer): ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"input":"hello","max_tokens":64}'
```

DeployBot: automatic-failover: routed traffic from us-east-1 -> eu-west-1 at 2024-06-06T14:02:12Z due to regional-saturation(us-east-1).

Rajat (Eng-SRE): quick summary of what likely happened: when us-east saturated our routing kicked failover to eu-west; eu-west had capacity but we also enforce a cross-region burst pool (global_burst_pool) for noisy tenants to avoid capacity hogging. the global pool can cause per-org cross-region throttles when a sudden multi-thousand-rps spike occurs.

Rajat (Eng-SRE): the headers you saw (`x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0`) are consistent with hitting the per-org regional token bucket + the global burst allowance drained. we throttle early to protect SLOs in that region.

Lina (Platform): adding detail: for hosted API the routing policy is: prefer region with lowest latency, but if region returns high saturation we failover. failover is immediate but we don't automatically increase the target org's regional quota; we rely on the global burst pool to absorb short spikes. if the spike > pool size you see 429s in the target region even though the region overall has spare capacity — it's intentional to avoid noisy neighbor issues.

Maya (Billing): quick check — your monthly committed quota? ken, looks like you are on the pay-as-you-go plan, no reserved dedicated capacity. that means you are subject to cross-org burst guards.

Ava (Support): actionable repro steps for our engineers: 1) reproduce by sending a 3–5k rps short-burst to us-east, then immediately switch all traffic to eu-west (simulate failover); 2) collect `x-rw-*` headers and routing logs from the console (Console -> Routes -> rw-corp-402 -> Traffic); 3) capture `route_decision` traces from tracing endpoint.

Ava (Support): example prod response we asked Ken to capture (copied from their log):
```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RW-Region: eu-west-1
X-RW-Rate-Limit-Remaining: 0
X-RW-Rate-Limit-Global-Burst: 0
Retry-After: 10

{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"global burst pool exhausted for org"}
```

Rajat (Eng-SRE): recommended immediate mitigations for customer: - client-side token bucket limiter + exponential backoff + jitter - prefer region pinning to keep traffic in origin region instead of automated failover if you can tolerate some latency - reduce instantaneous fanout (stagger requests across instances).

Rajat (Eng-SRE): medium-term we can: - temporarily raise your per-org regional quota for rw-corp-402 in eu-west-1 (manual override) - increase global burst pool size (ops decision, higher risk) - offer Dedicated reservation for predictable capacity.

Lina (Platform): I've checked Console metrics: there was a spike at 14:01 UTC on eu-west that consumed ~95% of the customer's regional tokens and drained their burst allocation. I'll open a ticket to request a temporary regional quota bump for rw-corp-402.

Maya (Billing): if we do a temporary bump we should flag as a one-off and review billing implications. ken, do you want us to enable a one-time quota increase for the next 2 hours to get you stable?

Ken (Customer): yes please that would help while we add client-side backoff. Also can you confirm if the global burst pool is shared across accounts in the same org or across all hosted customers? I couldn't find that in docs.

Rajat (Eng-SRE): global_burst_pool is shared across hosted customers in the same region and constrained by overall safety limits. it's not per-org — it's a shared emergency buffer with per-org caps. docs: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/multi-region-throttle (internal).

Ava (Support): next steps / action items: 
- Lina: request temporary regional quota bump for rw-corp-402 in eu-west-1 (+2x for 2 hours) — IN PROGRESS
- Maya: confirm billing notice and flag one-off invoice impact — ACTION
- Ken: implement client-side token bucket + jitter/backoff and pin to preferred region if possible — REQ
- Rajat: add a short-term runbook blurb for support to explain cross-region burst behavior and steps to request bump — ACTION

Ken (Customer): thanks folks — please keep me posted in this thread. appreciate the quick triage. :folded_hands:

Ava (Support): will do — tagging this as escalated to eng and ops. Ill update when the regional bump is active. :white_check_mark:
